title: Deadlock: the container goes quiet instead of busy

problem.summary: Threads take locks in conflicting orders and park forever. The giveaway is the opposite of what people look for: the container produces FEWER events than an idle one, because blocked threads make no syscalls.
symptoms: a service stops responding rather than slowing down
its CPU use falls instead of rising
requests time out rather than returning late

discriminators.this_problem: 70-84 events/s (n=5). Quieter than an idle container
discriminators.not_this_problem: lock contention runs 62,780-63,647 events/s with the same mechanism family - a factor of 800. Anything busy is not this
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on 41 labelled runs across 8 families with blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py (22-09-2026). deadlock 70-84 events/s (n=5) against lock_contention 62,780-63,647 (n=5), priority_inversion 19,439-19,632 (n=5), conn_pool_exhaustion 545-550 (n=5).

discriminators.signal: futex share, which is LOW here and not high
discriminators.this_problem: 4.3% (n=5) - the locks were taken once and never contended again
discriminators.not_this_problem: lock contention 47.0% and priority inversion 41.0%. A high futex share rules this out, which is the reverse of the intuition
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on 41 labelled runs across 8 families with blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py (22-09-2026). 4.3% (n=5) against 47.0% and 41.0% (n=5 each).

discriminators.signal: what little it does do is file operations
discriminators.this_problem: file ops 22.1% (n=5) - close, fcntl and openat2, which is the respawn loop opening and closing its lock files
discriminators.not_this_problem: no other family exceeds 0.6% on file ops. It is 0.0% for lock contention and priority inversion
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on 41 labelled runs across 8 families with blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py (22-09-2026). file ops 22.1% (n=5) against 0.0% for lock_contention and priority_inversion, 0.6% anomaly_mem, 0.1% noisy_neighbor.

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: a deadlock can be told from a crashed or stopped container
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: both look like a container that stops doing work. We measured the deadlock family only; no stopped-container family was measured against it.
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: state the ambiguity in the verdict. Distinguishing them needs process exit events or the container's own logs.

reproduction.teardown: the recipe restores state; verify against /sys/fs/cgroup
harness_only: the fault is injected as a sidecar container, which is a property of our harness. In production the same mechanism occurs inside an existing service - so the SHAPE transfers, the newcomer shortcut does not

collection_order.why_these: MEASURED BASIS. Every discriminator in this blueprint is a share of these event groups within one container. Nothing else in the trace is required, and no other modality is used - this blueprint was built and validated on kernel traces alone.

processing.expect: a CTF directory with metadata and channel streams

processing.step: Find containers that are active during the window and absent before it
processing.expect: one container with substantial traffic during the window and none before. If none appears, this blueprint does not apply - say so and stop

processing.step: Measure what share of its own events that container spends on each kind of work
processing.expect: the share profile below, within the measured range

processing.step: Apply the rules and emit the verdict
processing.expect: a verdict naming the container and the mechanism, or an explicit abstain
one page showing the shares, the cut, and what was ruled out

outputs.contains: culprit container pid_ns, its event shares, and the shares of every other container for comparison
per-container event shares for the window
each family's measured share on the deciding axis, with this run's value marked

verdict_when: a container is new to the window
its share profile matches the measured range below
no sibling container shows the same profile

rule_out.when: the container is busy - tens of thousands of events per second with futex near 47%
it is quiet but its events are network and ioctl rather than file operations

decision.root_cause_is: the container that appeared and then went nearly silent

provenance.authored_by: measured from StrataTrace v2 kernel traces
provenance.notes: Built 22-09-2026 from blueprints/lib/fingerprint_table.py over 41 labelled runs of 8 families. Candidate signals were first put through discover_signature.py (a specificity sweep across families, which rejected unlinkat, ftruncate, block_split, lseek and dup as window artefacts) and who_makes_it.py (which rejected the nagle_delayed_ack host-wide signal as 94% our own load generator). KERNEL TRACES ONLY - no metrics, logs or spans were consulted.

apply_when: a service stopped responding rather than slowing
its resource use fell rather than rose
do_not_apply_when: the suspect container is busy - that is contention, not deadlock
no container went quiet during the window
applicability.cheap_precheck: a container appeared in the window and produces under a few hundred events per second while the application is under load

stopping_conditions.conclude: the share profile matches and no sibling container matches it too
stopping_conditions.stop_and_switch: a discriminating share falls outside its measured range
stopping_conditions.stop_insufficient: no container is new to the window and none stands out

applicable_symptoms: a service stops responding rather than slowing down
its CPU use falls instead of rising
requests time out rather than returning late

historical_effectiveness.note: shares measured on 5 runs of this family

evidence_sufficiency.if_below_floor: report the shares and say which blueprint they sit between
evidence_sufficiency.report_when_stuck: the container's shares and every sibling's, side by side
